title: Traction Force Microscopy to Study B Lymphocyte Activation
protocol: Activate the coverslip or glass-bottom Petri dish with a UV lamp for 2 min.
Silanize the coverslip/glass-bottom dish using 200 µL aminopropyltrimethoxysilane (APTMS) for 5 min.
Wash the coverslip/glass-bottom dish thoroughly with ultra-pure water.
Dry the coverslip/glass-bottom dish using vacuum aspiration.
Place the coverslips into a ceramic coverslip holder.
Put the coverslip holder into a small beaker and pour siliconizing reagent over the coverslips to cover them completely.
Incubate the beaker covered with aluminum foil for 3 min at room temperature.
Transfer the coverslip holder with coverslips to a large beaker filled with ultra-pure water after 3 min of incubation in siliconizing reagent.
Rinse the coverslips thoroughly with ultra-pure water and dry them well.
Mix 75 µL of 40% acrylamide with 30 µL of 2% bisacrylamide (crosslinker) for gel polymerization.
Add 895 µL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) to the mixture.
Store the premix at 4 °C for up to one month.
To 167 µL of 0.5 kPa gel premix, add 1.67 µL of beads.
Vortex the mix and sonicate for 5 min in a bath sonicator with power of 50–100 W and frequency 40 kHz.
Protect the mix from light using aluminum foil.
Add 1.67 µL of 10% w/v ammonium persulfate (APS) to catalyze polymerization.
Add 0.2 µL of N,N,N′,N′-Tetramethylethylenediamine (TEMED) to initiate polymerization.
Mix with a pipette.
Pipette 9 µL of gel mix onto each coverslip/glass-bottom dish in the center.
Place the silanized/hydrophobic coverslip and flatten the gel.
Press the coverslip using forceps to ensure the gel spreads across the entire area until it starts leaking out.
Invert the coverslip/glass-bottom dish into a large Petri dish and tap it on the bench to push beads towards the gel surface.
Cover with aluminum foil and leave for 1 h to polymerize at room temperature in a humid chamber.
After 1 h, add PBS to the sample to facilitate coverslip release.
Remove the coverslip using a needle carefully.
Leave the gel in PBS.
Prepare Sulfo SANPAH solution at 0.5 mg/mL in 10 mM HEPES buffer.
Store Sulfo SANPAH solution at 4°C covered with aluminum foil for up to one week.
Aspirate the PBS from gels.
Add 150 µL of Sulfo SANPAH to the gel at room temperature.
Expose the gel to UV treatment for 2 min.
Wash the gel with PBS three times.
Repeat steps involving adding Sulfo SANPAH, exposing to UV, and washing the gel.
Add 250 µL of HEL (100 µg/mL) to each gel.
Incubate gels overnight in a humid chamber at 4°C while keeping covered with aluminum foil.

Remove PBS from the gels and add 500 µL of B cell media (RPMI 1640, 10% decomplemented fetal calf serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 2% Sodium Pyruvate, 50uM Mercaptoethanol and 1X Non Essential Amino Acids).
Let the gels equilibrate to room temperature.
Purify primary B cells from spleen according to a negative selection protocol.
Concentrate purified B cells to 3 x 106 cells/mL in B cell medium (RPMI-1640 supplemented with 10% fetal calf serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 0.1% mercaptoethanol and 2% sodium pyruvate).
Store cells as needed for up to 6 h at 4 °C.
Keep the cells at 37 °C for 30 min before image acquisition.
Use a confocal microscope with thermal and (possibly) CO2 control.
Focus on the gel plane using an objective/pinhole that allows a pixel size <200 nm.
Program the acquisition for 30 min with a frame rate of 5 s.
Aspirate the media from the gel, leaving about 200 µL of media on the gel.
Position the gel on the microscope and find the surface layer of beads and a nice even area on the gel.
Add 80 µL of cells (avoid touching the gel to maintain focus).
Ensure that the focus is still correct and that cells can be seen descending in the area under transmitted light.
Launch the acquisition before the cells reach the gel.
Adjust the focus if there is accidental contact with the gel, vibrations, or focus drift.
Collect an image of the relaxed gel before the arrival of the cells on the gel.
Prepare fluorescent HEL by binding a fluorescent dye (of a color different from the beads).
Acquire images with low illumination settings or low frame rate to avoid photo-bleaching.
Compute the intensity integrated over the cell area for each frame I(t) corrected and normalized by the intensity I(0) of frame 0.
Obtain fluorescent B cells by purifying B cells from the spleens of genetically modified mice as done for wild type mice.
Use a spinning disk microscope with a water immersion long-distance 40x–100x objective for imaging.
Keep exposure duration and frame rate low to avoid bleaching.
Correct the whole stack for drift.
Find beads in each frame.
Track bead movements with respect to a reference frame taken without cells.
Interpolate the displacement field.
Invert the problem using Fourier transform to obtain stress.
Open the movie in ImageJ as a stack of images.
Run the macro “Crop_and_save.ijm”.
Select regions of interest (ROI) using the “Rectangle” tool and add them to the ROI list.
Include at least 5–10 pixels of immobile beads when cropping the cell.
Exclude cells that are too close to boundaries or other cells from analysis.
Click on ‘OK’ after selecting satisfactory ROIs; if not, manually select a closed region with any selection tool and click on “Continue”.
Open MATLAB and run “TFM_v1.m”.
Input required parameters including image properties (pixel size, time interval of acquisition) and gel properties (Young modulus E, Poisson ratio).
